checks: The generating compact union is contained in the old convex set and includes all old integer fibers, so its hull preserves those fibers. This argument applies to every allowed affine dimension.

Actual Minkowski compatibility gives discrete concavity of each directional support sequence. Adjacent interpolation is concave, so every convex representation of a real base gives a weighted support at most the interpolant. The adjacent pair is feasible and attains the interpolant in every direction, proving fiber equality.

Adding the supports at u and −u makes the real-fiber width the adjacent affine interpolation of integer widths. The maximum real width is therefore attained at an integer fiber. The vertical section of the compact convex difference body consists of same-real-base differences, so its support is exactly this maximum, matching the sampled difference hull.
The one-fiber case is direct. The original opening theorem (1)–(2) applies to the canonical hull and does not retain arbitrary off-lattice bulges of the old body.

Its binary four-coordinate witness has distinct sampled and same-real-base difference bodies. It does not affect equality in one integer coordinate.
